rows.author: K016;I078;I081;K126;K106;I058;K053;K027;J082;K099;K142;J086;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR GENDER-BASED SEXUAL HARASSMENT IN THE WORKPLACE AND IN EDUCATIONAL AND TRAINING INSTITUTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11313, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “SAFE SPACES ACT”
rows.title_short: Providing Penalties For Gender - Based Sexual Harassment In The Workplace And In Educational And Training Institutions, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 11313, Otherwise Known As The “ Safe Spaces Act ”
rows.abstract:
Imposes the penalty of prision correccional in its maximum period, or a fine of not less than two hundred fifty thousand pesos (P250, 000.00) but not more than five hundred thousand pesos (P500, 000.00) or both upon any person found guilty of any gender-based sexual harassment, at the discretion of the court.
States that if the perpetrator is the head of the workplace or organization, the appointment of such person shall be deemed revoked upon conviction.
Declares that an alien who commits gender-based sexual harassment in the workplace shall be subject to deportation proceedings after serving a sentence and/or payment of fines.
Penalizes any public official or government employee who is found guilty of fomenting, promoting, or exhorting acts of sexual harassment, misogynistic, transphobic, homophobic, and sexist slurs, either verbally, in writing, or through digital or social media platform. 
Provides that if the perpetrator is the head of the educational or training institution or organization, the appointment if such person shall be deemed revokes upon conviction, and if an alien commits gender-based sexual harassment in an educational or training institution, said alien shall be subject to deportation proceedings after serving a sentence and/or payment of fines.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SOCIALIZED AND LOW-COST HOUSING LOAN RESTRUCTURING AND CONDONATION PROGRAM
rows.title_short: Socialized And Low - Cost Housing Loan Restructuring And Condonation Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to make available at affordable cost decent housing and basic services to underprivileged and homeless citizens.
Condones all socialized and low-cost housing loans with the NHA and SHFC that have at least three (3) months of unpaid monthly amortizations for a period of twenty-four (24) months after the issuance of the implementing rules and regulations of this Act. 
Authorizes the NHA and SHFC to continue the loan restructuring and condonation program notwithstanding the lapse of twenty-four months application period.
Allows restructuring of housing loans and the assumption of payment of outstanding loan by the legal heirs and successors-in-interest.
Provides incentives to all accounts which monthly amortization are paid on time.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE LEGAL EDUCATION BOARD, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7662, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "LEGAL EDUCATION REFORM ACT OF 1993", AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Revised Legal Education Reform Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to undertake reforms in the legal education system that shall require the proper selection of law students, maintain quality among law schools, and require legal apprenticeship and continuing legal education.
Creates the Commission on Legal Education (CLED) which shall formulate development plans, policies, priorities and programs on legal education and research, and implement the same under the provisions of this Act, or in the absence of such provisions, to recommend to the Legislative Branch appropriate remedial legislation.
Provides that law schools may not operate unless accredited by the CLED, and accreditation of law schools may be granted only to those recognized by the government and whose charters or articles of incorporation expressly or impliedly authorize them to offer law courses.
Creates the Legal Education Fund (FUND) which shall be under the control of the CLED and to be used exclusively for the improvement and strengthening of legal education in the entire country.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING EDUCATION PATHWAYS FOR BASIC EDUCATION STUDENTS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Education Pathways Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to ensure opportunities for Filipinos to attain maximum potential and enhance their employability by establishing inclusive education pathways that empower and equip the learners with the competencies that are necessary for college or employment.
Provides two education pathways for completers of Junior High School: the University Preparatory Program under the Department of Education (DepEd) of the Technical-Vocational Program under the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA).
Mandates the DepEd to develop and implement a comprehensive curriculum for Grades 11 and 12 that prepares students for admission to colleges and universities and to include the University Preparatory Pathway in its education roadmap in collaboration with the CHED, colleges, and universities to guarantee alignment between curriculum and college admission standards.
Mandates the TESDA and the industry boards, partners, experts, and practitioners, including small and medium enterprises, to develop and offer a variety of technical-vocational programs based on an industry-driver and industry-approved curriculum that is designed to equip students with practical skills and competencies that are at par with industry standards.
Allows students who finished the technical-vocational program and successfully qualifying in the Philippine Educational Placement Test conducted by DepEd for Grades 11 and 12 or any equivalent assessment administered by the Dep Ed to enroll in colleges or universities and avail of the ladderized education program for educational advancement.
Directs the DepEd and TESDA to maintain an educational support program including scholarships for their respective students that properly and sufficiently addresses the accessibility and availability of the pathways to the marginalized communities and learners.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2025-01-28, transmitted to the Senate on 2025-01-30 and received by the Senate on 2025-01-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PRIVATE BASIC EDUCATION VOUCHER PROGRAM, PROVIDING FOR THE CREATION OF THE BUREAU OF PRIVATE EDUCATION, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 2, 3, 4(2), 4(3), 5, 6, 7, 12, 14, AND 15 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8545, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "EXPANDED GOVERNMENT ASSISTANCE TO STUDENTS AND TEACHERS IN PRIVATE EDUCATION ACT", WHICH AMENDED REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6728, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "GOVERNMENT ASSISTANCE TO STUDENTS AND TEACHERS IN PRIVATE EDUCATION ACT"
rows.title_short: Private Basic Education Vouchers Assistance Act
rows.abstract:
Covers all private basic education institutions that receive government assistance in the form of vouchers for qualified students, teachers and schools.
Provides criteria for voucher assistance for students and schools.
Mandates the Department of Education to establish, operate and maintain a system and mechanism for monitoring program outcomes to ensure accountability of participating recognized private basic educational institutions.
Provides other forms of assistance to teachers and qualified recognized private education schools.
Allows schools participating in the basic education voucher program to increase tuition on the condition that seventy percent (70%) of the amount of tuition increases shall go to the payment of salaries, wages, allowances, and other statutory benefits of teaching and non-teaching personnel and twenty percent (20%) of the tuition increases shall go to the improvement or modernization of buildings, equipment, libraries, laboratories, gymnasia and similar facilities and to the payment of other costs of operation.
Establishes the Inset Fund in the DepEd to provide for training programs for the upgrading of knowledge and teaching competencies in critical subject areas and for the modernization of teaching techniques and strategies, and the Teacher´s Salary Subsidy Fund.
Creates the Bureau of Private Education to serve as the focal office for the administration, supervision, and regulation of all matters relating to private basic education institutions, including government assistance and subsidies.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ENSURING THE FUNDAMENTAL EQUALITY OF MEN AND WOMEN UNDER THE LAWS ON MARRIAGE AND FAMILY RELATIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 14, 96, 124, 211 AND 225 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES"
rows.title_short: Ensuring The Fundamental Equality Of Men And Women Under The Laws On Marriage And Family Relations, Amending For The Purpose Articles 14, 96, 124, 211 And 225 Of Executive Order No. 209, Otherwise Known As The " Family Code Of The Philippines "
rows.abstract:
Seeks correct the inequitable and unfair situation under the current law which mandates that the decision of the father should prevail on matters relating to marriage and family relations.
Mandates that either parent, or guardian, or the person who has legal charge of either or both contracting parties for marriage between the ages of eighteen and twenty-one shall give consent to the marriage.
States that any act of administration of the community property and conjugal partnership by either spouse without the consent of the other shall be unenforceable until it subsequently ratified by the non-consenting spouse and that in case of disagreement, the spouses shall make earnest efforts to settle their differences.
Provides that the State shall consider the best interest of the family, damages and expenses of litigation in deciding the case of spouses who fail to enter into compromise regarding the administration of community property and conjugal partnership.
States that any exercise of guardianship by either parent of the minor child without the consent of the other shall be unenforceable until it is subsequently ratified by the non-consenting parent and that in case of disagreement, either parent shall have recourse to the court within five (5) years from the date the contract was entered by the parties or upon knowledge of the non-consenting parent, whichever comes later.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA OF TRICYCLE DRIVERS AND OPERATORS AND INSTITUTIONALIZING THE MECHANISMS FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION
rows.title_short: Magna Carta Of Tricycle Drivers And Operators
rows.abstract:
Seeks to mandate a uniform rules which provides cities and municipalities the power to regulate the operation of tricycles and grant permits subject to the guidelines prescribed by the Department of Transportation (DOTr), Land Transportation Office (LTO), and the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB).
Provides a simple system and procedure for registration and issuance of Motorizes Tricycle Operators Permit (MTOP).
Mandates LGUs to establish a Tricycle Sector One-Stop Shop which shall handle all transactions and processing of the business permit applications within their respective jurisdictions.
Enumerate the rights and benefits of workers in the tricycle sector.
Seeks to provide and extend affordable insurance, social security and health care coverage to the tricycle sector.
Provides a policy on impounding of tricycles.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING THE INTERMENT OF FILIPINO SPORTS HEROES AT THE LIBINGAN NG MGA BAYANI
rows.title_short: Commemoration Of Filipino Sports Heroes Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to honor and perpetuate the memory of the Filipino sports heroes who have led lives worthy of inspiration and emulation through generations.
Refers to sports heroes as “Filipino athletes, amateur or professional, including athletes with disabilities, who have distinguished themselves in their particular field of sports, possessed good moral character and integrity, represented and brought honor and glory to the country by winning any medal in the Olympics or Paralympic Games or a World Championship.”
Includes any Filipino athlete, coach, or trainer who were inducted into the Philippine Sports Hall of Fame pursuant to Republic Act No. 8757, entitled “An Act Establishing the Philippine Sports Hall of Fame and Appropriating Funds Therefor”.
Requires sports heroes to be citizens of the Philippines or former Filipino citizens by birth who are naturalized in another country but re-acquired Philippine citizenship pursuant to Republic Act No. 9225 of the “Citizenship Retention and Re-acquisition Act of 2003”.
Establishes a screening committee to determine and recommend qualified Filipino sports heroes.
Mandates the PSC or the GAB to coordinate with the AFP to issue the interment directive and make the necessary arrangements for the interment service.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NEW CHARTER OF THE DEVELOPMENT BANK OF THE PHILIPPINES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 81, DATED DECEMBER 3, 1986, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE 1986 REVISED CHARTER OF THE DEVELOPMENT BANK OF THE PHILIPPINES", AS AMENDED
rows.title_short: The New Development Bank Of The Philippines ( D B P ) Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to strengthen the powers and functions of the Development Bank of the Philippines as the country´s premier government developmental financial institution that provides developmental financing and financial services necessary for the achievement of sustained economic growth.
Provides for the composition as well as the powers and functions of the Bank which shall be vested in and exercised by a Board of Directors composed of nine (9) members as follows: a.) The Secretary of Finance as the ex-officio Chairperson of the Board; b.) The Secretary of the National Economic and Development Authority, as an ex-officio member; c.) Four (4) regular directors and three (3) independent directors to be appointed by the President of the Philippines in accordance with the appointment process and the Fit and Proper Rule under RA 10149.Exempts all collaterals, securities and loan guarantees and other accommodations granted by the Bank or its predecessors-in-interest from attachment, execution, stay order, or any other court processes, nor shall these be subject to insolvency proceedings unless all debts to the Bank have been previously paid.
Prohibits the unauthorized exaction of fee, commission, gift, or charge of any kind for obtaining loans from the Bank.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 4 AND 9 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7309, ENTITLED “AN ACT CREATING A BOARD OF CLAIMS UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE FOR VICTIMS OF UNJUST IMPRISONMENT OR DETENTION AND VICTIMS OF VIOLENT CRIMES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
rows.abstract:
Proposes to amend the amount of compensation that victims can receive for up to P50,000.00 per month, to raise the maximum amount of claims to P500,000.00, and introduce a provision that automatically reviews the compensation amounts every three years.
States that “THE BOARD SHALL . . . REVIEW AND WHEN NECESSARY ADJUST THE AMOUNT OF THE AWARD CEILING . . . TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE PRESENT CONSUMER PRICE INDEX AS PUBLISHED BY THE PHILIPPINE STATISTICS AUTHORITY (PSA) AND OTHER RELEVANT ECONOMIC INDICATORS, . . .
Seeks to increase the subsequent annual funding to THREE PERCENT (3%) of the net income of the PAGCOR and THREE PERCENT (3%) of the proceeds and sales and other disposition and military camps in Metro Manila by the Bases Conversion and Development Authority.

rows.author: E003;F027;K032;K063;G002;E045;G059;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF COCKPITS AND OTHER STRUCTURES OR FACILITIES FOR HOLDING COCKFIGHTS WITHIN A RADIUS OF FIVE HUNDRED LINEAL METERS FROM ANY EXISTING RESIDENTIAL OR COMMERCIAL AREA, SCHOOLS AND OTHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, CHURCH BUILDINGS AND OTHER PLACES OF WORSHIP, AND HOSPITALS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.title_short: Cockpit Regulation Law Of 2024
rows.abstract:
Prohibits the following when done or conducted within a radius of five hundred (500) lineal meters from any existing residential or commercial area, school or other educational institution, church building or other place of worship, or hospital: 1.) Construction, operation or managing of a cockpit or other building, structure or facility intended to be used for holding cockfights; and 2.) The betting or collecting bets in or participating in any other manner in the conduct of a cockfight.
Declares it also illegal, prohibited, and punishable under this Act the following: 1.) Approving, issuing, or facilitating in any manner the approval or issuance, of permits to construct, make or erect, cockpits, or other buildings, structures or facilities intended for holding cockfights within the prohibited place; and 2.) Approving, issuing or facilitating in any manner the approval or issuance of permits to conduct or hold cockfights in such cockpits, buildings, structures or facilities or other prohibited place.
Prohibits government employees and public officials from committing any of the prohibited acts provided by this Act.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2025-06-04, transmitted to the Senate on 2025-06-09 and received by the Senate on 2025-06-09

rows.author: F057;J117;K122;K039;K032;K063;G002;J044;J037;F027;J024;H057;E045;H038;K083;K025;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING ANY ACTIVITY RELATED TO ONLINE COCKFIGHTING OR E-SABONG OPERATIONS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.title_short: Prohibiting Any Activity Related To Online Cockfighting Or E-sabong Operations And Providing Penalties For Violation
rows.abstract:
Seeks to prohibit and penalize the following acts: 1.) Online, remote, or off-site wagering or betting on live cockfighting matches, events, and activities streamed or broadcasted live from cockpit arenas or premises where the activity is being held; 2.) place, receive or transmit a bet wager on live-streaming or broadcasting of live cockfighting matches, events or activities through online or other remote mode of betting; or 3.) Operate or maintain e-sabong betting platform.
Declares invalid all permits and licenses of e-sabong operators issued by the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR) upon the effectivity of this Act.
Mandates the National Telecommunications Commission, Cybercrime Division of the National Bureau of Investigation, Anti-Cybercrime Group of the Philippine National Police, Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center of the Department of Information and Communications Technology, and other law enforcement agencies to monitor and block all existing and emerging e-sabong websites.

rows.author: F068;G066;I016;K106;K105;F088;K034;F057;J102;C102;J012;J043;K078;K020;K025;J047;K035;J046;K009;K058;G050;
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE PHILIPPINE POSTAL CORPORATION TO ADOPT A MODERNIZED ZONE IMPROVEMENT PLAN CODE SYSTEM
rows.title_short: Modernized Zip Code System Act
rows.abstract:
Mandates the Philippine Postal Corporation (PHLPOST) to adopt and institutionalize a modernized alphanumeric Zone Improvement Plan (ZIP) Code that shall be compose of: two (2) alphabetic characters (A-Z),  representing the province; and five (5) Arabic numerals (0-9), representing the city or municipality and barangay.
Directs the PHLPOST to update its website´s ZIP Code Locator that shall allow the public to search with ease the ZIP Code of a certain barangay and vice versa.
Provides a thirty-six (36) months transitory period from the effectivity of this Act for all national government agencies, local government units, government-owned or -controlled corporations, and private sector entities to update their database using the new ZIP Code System.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 144, 145, 147 AND 263-A OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to grant a suspension of one year to the automatic annual increase of five percent (5%) of tax imposed among tobacco products, heated tobacco products, vapor products, cigars, and cigarettes.

Intends to lower the price gap between a legitimate cigarette product compared to illicit cigarettes to encourage consumers to shift to purchasing legitimate products.

Seeks to address the proliferation of mislabeled vapor products to evade the imposition of higher taxes, resulting in millions of excise taxes lost by illicit traders and the growing threats of illicit tobacco trafficking/smuggling.
rows.status: Substituted by HB11360

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE INCLUSION OF AUTOMATIC OR PRE-SELECTED ADD-ONS TO ONLINE TRANSACTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7394, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "CONSUMER ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES"
rows.abstract:
Aims to uphold the Filipino consumer´s right to make informed choices by proposing additional circumstances to determine whether an act or practice is unfair and unconscionable:

“F) THAT THE SELLER OR SUPPLIER EMPLOYS AGGRESSIVE MARKETING PRACTICES INCLUDING AUTOMATIC OR PRE-SELECTED ADD-ONS TO ONLINE TRANSACTIONS THAT SIGNIFICANTLY CONSTRAIN OR IMPAIR THE CONSUMER´S FREEDOM OF CHOICE WITH REGARD TO THE PURCHASE OF A PRODUCT OR SERVICE, AND CAUSE THE CONSUMER TO MAKE UNITENDED EXPENSES OR ENTER INTO A TRANSACTION DIFFERENT FROM THE ONE THAT THE CONSUMER INTENDED, OR A TRANSACTION THE CONSUMER WOULD NOT HAVE AVAILED OF IF CHOICES WERE PRESENTED.”

rows.title_short: Strengthening The Administration Of Excise Tax On Tobacco Products, Cigars, Cigarettes, Heated Tobacco Products, Vapor Products And Novel Tobacco Products, Amending For The Purpose The National Internal Revenue Code Of 1997
rows.abstract: Seeks to impose heavy and differentiated penalties based on the degree of involvement in illicit trade on tobacco and other related products; establish a modern digital tracking and tracing system for the manufacturing, importation, storage, removal, distribution, and sale of tobacco and related products; form an inter-agency body to facilitate information sharing and collaborative enforcement among government agencies and stakeholders; broaden the scope of activities that fall under illicit tobacco trade; and strengthen monitoring by mandating the conduct of regular surveys to determine the magnitude of illicit trade.

rows.title_full: AN ACT FIXING THE TERM OF OFFICE OF BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN OFFICIALS AND CHANGING THE TERM OF OFFICE FROM THREE (3) YEARS TO SIX (6) YEARS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 42 AND 43 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AS AMENDED
rows.title_short: Fixing The Term Of Office Of Barangay And Sangguniang Kabataan Officials And Changing The Term Of Office From Three (3) Years To Six (6) Years, Amending For The Purpose Sections 42 And 43 Of Republic Act No. 7160, Otherwise Known As The Local Government Code Of 1991
rows.abstract:
Sets the synchronized Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections on the second Monday of May 2029 and every six (6) years thereafter.
Extends the term of office of Barangay officials and Sangguniang Kabataan from three (3) years to six (6) years.
Prohibits elective Barangay official to serve for more than two (2) consecutive terms in the same position.
States that voluntary renunciation of the office for any length of time shall not be considered as an interruption in the continuity of service for the full term for which the elective Barangay official concerned was elected.
Prohibits elective Sangguniang Kabataan official to serve for more than one (1) term.  
Provides that all incumbent Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials elected last October 30, 2023 shall remain in office unless sooner removed or suspended for cause.
rows.status: Republic Act RA12232 enacted on 2025-08-13
